explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - Falco is a C++-based, cloud-native Linux runtime security tool that monitors kernel events (syscalls) and container metadata, applies user-defined rules, and emits alerts in real time.  
   - It comprises a kernel-space component (drivers/BPF), a userspace engine (event capture, filtering, rule evaluation), and a userspace daemon/CLI (`falco`) providing gRPC/HTTP interfaces and various output plugins.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top-level build orchestration: `CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/` modules, `Makefile`, Docker and CI workflows (`.github/workflows/`, `docker/`).  
   - Core libraries (event capture, rule engine) live under `userspace/engine/`.  
   - The Falco daemon/application (CLI, servers, output plugins) lives under `userspace/falco/`.  
   - Configuration and default rule files in `config/`.  
   - Packaging scripts under `scripts/`.  
   - Demo and containerized environment in `docker/docker-compose/`.

3. README insights  
   - Falco uses backends for driver loading (kernel module or modern BPF) provided via `libs` submodule.  
   - Outputs can be to stdout, file, syslog, HTTP, gRPC or via plugins (Falco Plugin SDK).  
   - Offers a gRPC server and embedded HTTP server for remote control and event streaming.  
   - Demo environment includes Falco, Falcosidekick (event shipper), Redis, and UI.

4. Main components & their interactions  
   a. Kernel-space probes (legacy kmod or eBPF):  
      • Capture raw syscall/container events  
      • Built via CMake modules (`cmake/modules/bpf.cmake`, `driver.cmake`)  
   b. Event Capture Library (`libscap` in `userspace/engine/`):  
      • Reads events from kernel probe  
      • Normalizes, buffers, and hands off to engine  
   c. Falco Engine (`userspace/engine/`):  
      • Applies filter rules, resolves macros, tracks stats  
      • Generates alerts and enriches events with metadata (e.g., Kubernetes)  
   d. Falco Daemon/CLI (`userspace/falco/app/`):  
      • Loads engine, handles CLI commands (`run`, `list`, `start_grpc_server`, etc.)  
      • Manages lifecycle, signal handling, config parsing  
   e. Output Plugins & Servers (`userspace/falco/outputs*`, `grpc_server`, `webserver`):  
      • Formats and dispatches alerts to stdout, files, syslog, HTTP POST, gRPC streams  
      • Embedded HTTP/gRPC servers to stream events to clients or orchestration tools  
   f. External Components:  
      • Container runtime/Kubernetes API for metadata enrichment  
      • SIEM/Data Lake or Falcosidekick (via Docker Compose) as downstream consumers  

5. Architectural patterns & design principles  
   - Layered architecture: kernel probe → capture library → engine → output layer  
   - Modular CMake organization for drivers, third-party libs, static analysis  
   - Plugin-style outputs and server interfaces for extensibility  
   - Single-process, single-thread execution model in Falco daemon for deterministic behavior  

6. Guidelines for tailoring the diagram  
   - Emphasize clear separation of layers:  
     • Kernel-space probes (lowest layer)  
     • Userspace engine (core processing)  
     • Daemon/CLI (control plane)  
     • Output & server interfaces (data plane)  
   - Highlight configuration and packaging artifacts: `config/`, `scripts/`, `docker/`  
   - If focusing on the demo environment, include the Docker Compose services: Falco container, Falcosidekick, Redis, UI  

7. Diagramming elements to include  
   - Components as labeled boxes or swimlanes, colored by layer:  
     • Kernel Probe (e.g., orange)  
     • Event Capture & Engine (blue)  
     • Falco Daemon & Servers (green)  
     • Output Plugins & External Consumers (purple)  
   - Directional arrows to show event flow:  
     Kernel → libscap → Engine → Outputs → External services  
   - Shapes for special roles:  
     • Cylinder for data stores (Redis in demo)  
     • Cloud icon for Kubernetes API or SIEM  
     • Gear icon for CMake build modules and scripts  

8. Detailed and comprehensive capture  
   - Include low-level build and packaging modules (`cmake/`, `scripts/`) as supporting elements  
   - Show submodules (e.g., `falcosecurity-libs`, `falcosecurity-rules`) as external dependencies  
   - Label ports and endpoints of the gRPC and HTTP servers  

By following this outline, you can produce a system design diagram that reflects Falco’s layered architecture, core components, data flow from kernel to external consumers, and its extensible plugin/output model. Be sure to annotate technologies (CMake, eBPF, gRPC, HTTP), code modules (userspace/engine vs userspace/falco), and packaging strategies (Docker Compose) so readers can trace implementation details directly to the file structure.  
</explanation>
